paragraphs: WebIZ is an immunization information system sold to state and local government public health agencies. The registry is now offered inside InductiveHealth's public health platform. It is built to meet CDC standards for tracking and administering immunizations in any jurisdiction.

The system follows vaccine inventory from ordering through delivery and administration. Clinic record systems send administered doses straight into the registry, which cuts duplicate entry. Embedded dashboards report coverage rates by ZIP code, vaccine type, age group and provider. School entry rules are configured once for a state and then applied to every student and grade. Residents pull their own immunization records from a secure portal with multi-factor authentication.

The company says the product has served more than 20 jurisdictions across two decades. Under a shared development model, one jurisdiction's funded enhancement reaches the rest in the next monthly release. InductiveHealth dates its founding to 2013. It works with federal, state, tribal, local and territorial jurisdictions on disease surveillance. Staff include epidemiologists and public health experts alongside engineers and technologists.

quote.text: Configure state-specific school entry requirements once and apply automatically to every student and every grade.
